title: On the Identifiability of User Adaptation in Co-Adaptive Neural Interfaces
summary:
madduri et al . [ 2 ] recently presented an elegant experimental and theoretical framework for study-ing co-adaptive neural interfaces , in which a human user and a machine decoder jointly adapt in closed - loop . 
 we show that while the empirical procedure recovers joint closed-loop dynamics , it does not , in general , uniquely identify the user-side adaptation mechanism . this distinction , though subtle , is quite important for inter-preting claims about predicting or shaping human behavior .
key_findings: The empirical procedure recovers joint closed-loop dynamics.
User-side adaptation mechanisms are not uniquely identifiable.
The distinction between recovery of dynamics and identification is crucial for interpreting human behavior.
methodology: The study employs an experimental and theoretical framework to analyze co-adaptive neural interfaces involving human users and machine decoders.
limitations: The user-side adaptation mechanism cannot be uniquely identified.
The framework may not account for all variables influencing adaptation.
future_work: Develop methods to uniquely identify user-side adaptation mechanisms.
Explore additional variables that may affect co-adaptive dynamics.
Investigate implications of non-unique identifiability on behavioral predictions.
